claims.statement: All 186 held orders belong to the EXC-0921 scope (v18-affected, split-reservation), and 100% of EXC-0921 orders routed to the east node are held.
claims.corroboration: Tier-1 verified audit result from Inventory Control directly confirms perfect correlation.
claims.limitation: Correlation is established, but the audit explicitly cannot separate an effect of the rule change from an effect on the east-node lanes, because only rule-affected orders were routed there. Causation is not yet discriminated.

claims.statement: The root cause is either (a) a defect in v18 allocation logic creating invalid reservations, or (b) a carrier feed lag or dock constraint on the east-node lanes preventing pickup despite valid allocations.
claims.corroboration: m8_r_exceptions audit limitation explicitly states this ambiguity: cannot separate rule-change effect from east-node-lane effect.
claims.limitation: Requires discriminating evidence: inventory count verification will show whether reservations are valid (supporting hypothesis b) or corrupted (supporting hypothesis a).

next_action.rationale: The audit confirms perfect correlation between v18-affected orders and held orders, but cannot discriminate whether v18 is creating valid or invalid reservations. Inspecting inventory counts will reveal whether the split reservations in EXC-0921 are legitimate (stock reserved correctly) or corrupted (inventory drift). If counts match allocations, the issue is carrier-side and rules can be preserved. If counts drift or conflict with allocations, v18 is creating invalid reservations and must be rolled back.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Direct evidence on whether v18's split-reservation logic is working correctly; this discriminates between the two root-cause hypotheses.
